subject: Thoughts on more informative progress info?

messages.author: dae01c57a3c54a3a
messages.subject: Thoughts on more informative progress info?
parts:
I was thinking of hacking together a modification of the current progress info printed during the operation of rstan::sampling() that, when the sample_file and diagnostic_file options are used (typically for high compute-time scenarios) will pull out useful information from those files as they are updated. For example, once warmup is done, it would show the n_eff & Rhat info (or some summary thereof if there are lots of parameters) as new samples come in. 

While I'm at it, is there any other information that might be useful to show as well? I'm not confident enough with my understanding of the warmup procedure to venture a guess at what might be useful from that period, but would certainly welcome any thoughts on this.

Cheers,

Mike

--
Mike Lawrence
Graduate Student
Department of Psychology & Neuroscience
Dalhousie University

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Thoughts on more informative progress info?
parts:
> On Aug 22, 2016, at 8:18 PM, Mike Lawrence <mike....@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> I was thinking of hacking together a modification of the current progress info printed during the operation of rstan::sampling() that, when the sample_file and diagnostic_file options are used (typically for high compute-time scenarios) will pull out useful information from those files as they are updated. For example, once warmup is done, it would show the n_eff & Rhat info (or some summary thereof if there are lots of parameters) as new samples come in.

All the stats for R-hat can be calculated online as draws come in,
but not for the split-R-hat we use. If you want to do that, it's
expensive to do on the fly and you wouldn't want to have sampling
block while waiting for diagnostics to compute.

With multiple chains, our algorithms require all the chains to
be the same length which you could do by simply ignoring the tails
of some.

Just counter of which chain is at which iteration would be useful
along with projected time to completion (that can be based on a rolling
average of time taken).

> While I'm at it, is there any other information that might be useful to show as well? I'm not confident enough with my understanding of the warmup procedure to venture a guess at what might be useful from that period, but would certainly welcome any thoughts on this.

From warmup, there's also the state of where the parameters are at
and also where the stepsize and mass matrix are at (usually diagonal).
When all chains are converging to the same place, stepsize and mass
matrices should be the same across chains.

- Bob
